description: Phase 6bo gate — three parser/compiler gaps from post-6bn random-corpus analysis: CROSS JOIN, ALL quantifier inside aggregate args, bare column references with GROUP BY.

program.sql: SELECT * FROM t CROSS JOIN u;

cases.name: cross-join-multi
cases.description: CROSS JOIN composes with comma-join equivalently.

program.sql: SELECT * FROM t CROSS JOIN u, v;

cases.name: cross-join-product
cases.description: CROSS JOIN produces full cartesian product.

program.sql: SELECT * FROM t CROSS JOIN u ORDER BY a, b;

cases.name: cross-join-with-alias
cases.description: Aliases on both sides of CROSS JOIN.

program.sql: SELECT x.a, y.a FROM t AS x CROSS JOIN t AS y ORDER BY x.a, y.a;

cases.name: agg-all-nested-unary
cases.description: ALL then unary + then expression, matching random corpus shape SUM(ALL (+ col2)).

cases.name: bare-column-group-by
cases.description: SQLite permits a bare column reference in SELECT when GROUP BY is present. To keep the value deterministic for cross-build equivalence, each group here has a single distinct col1 value, so bare-column emit is unambiguous.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (col0 INTEGER, col1 INTEGER);
SELECT col1 FROM t GROUP BY col0 ORDER BY col0;

cases.name: bare-column-group-by-with-agg
cases.description: Bare column + aggregate in same SELECT list alongside GROUP BY.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (col0 INTEGER, col1 INTEGER);
SELECT col0, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY col0 ORDER BY col0;

cases.name: bare-column-having
cases.description: Bare column in HAVING with GROUP BY — same relaxation applies.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (col0 INTEGER, col1 INTEGER);
SELECT col0 FROM t GROUP BY col0 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

cases.name: implicit-alias-lhs-cross-join
cases.description: Regression #111: implicit table alias on LHS of CROSS JOIN. `FROM a cor0 CROSS JOIN b AS cor1` must be accepted — CROSS is a valid follow-set token for an implicit alias.

program.sql: SELECT * FROM a cor0 CROSS JOIN b AS cor1;
